headline: Nifty slipped while *more stocks rose than fell*
subline: Reliance and Infosys weighed on the index. Autos, pharma and media ran.
hero_text: Nifty closed at 22,698.85, down 0.22%. IT and oil and gas dragged, while autos, pharma and the broader market held up.

why.title: IT dragged the index lower
why.desc: Infosys and Tech Mahindra fell, pulling Nifty IT down.

why.title: Autos ran ahead of the tape
why.desc: Autos topped the sector board, ahead of durables and media.

why.title: US markets gave mixed signals
why.desc: The S&P 500 rose while the Nasdaq slipped slightly.

sector_reasons.Auto: Led the board on a broad auto bid
sector_reasons.Consumer Durables: Rose alongside autos on a firm bid
sector_reasons.Media: Held a steady bid through the session
sector_reasons.Oil & Gas: Reliance and ONGC pulled it down
sector_reasons.IT: Infosys and Tech Mahindra led the slide

bonus_text: 1,430 stocks rose and 1,246 fell, so the tape beat the index. 26 of 50 Nifty names closed green.
movers_note_gainers: Apollo Hospitals led, with L&T and Trent close behind.
movers_note_losers: Infosys and Reliance led the slide, each down over 3%.
watch_text: Thursday: Nifty max pain sits at 22,700, right at the close. Max call OI is at 24,000, max put OI at 20,050.
lessons: Breadth beat the index. More stocks rose than fell even as Nifty slipped.
Two heavyweights capped the index. Reliance and Infosys fell over 3% each.
Size helped. Smallcaps rose while the frontline slipped.
Institutions agreed. FIIs and DIIs both bought in cash, yet the index still dipped.
alert_text: US GDP and Core PCE data and the ECB rate decision land Thursday evening IST.
cta_headline: Index down, tape up. *Bookmark the breadth check*.
cta_sub: Thursday opens with US GDP and the ECB decision due that evening.
next_text: Thursday 29 October opens next. US GDP and the ECB decision arrive in the evening IST.
caption_a:
Nifty slipped 0.22% to 22,698.85, yet more stocks rose than fell.
Advances beat declines 1,430 to 1,246. Autos rose 1.45% while IT fell 1.98%.
FIIs bought Rs 871.83 Cr and DIIs Rs 643.35 Cr.
Watch: US GDP and the ECB decision on Thursday.
